newsitem.title: UK: EU green rate changes seen on Aug 1, not July 31.
newsitem.headline: EU green rate changes seen on Aug 1, not July 31.

text.p: The next likely round of EU green rate changes will be on August 1, not July 31, according to the UK's Home Grown Cereals Authority.

This means that the current confirmation period will be 11 days long, rather than the usual ten. The change has been made by the European Commission so that the confirmation period ends, neatly, at the end of the month, the HGCA said.
On the basis of exchange rates in the period so far, the HGCA predicted changes for for the Belgian, German, Dutch, Danish, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Austrian green rates on August 1.
Also on August 1, sterling is slated to enter the fourth of a possible five confirmation periods ahead of a green rate revaluation which would take place on August 21.
Green rates are used by the European Union to convert Ecus into the currencies of its member states in its Common Agricultural Policy.
